messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 2061234567 — GPU OOMs detected on serving pool 'eu-west-1/gpu-pool-c'. Alerting oncall rotation.

mike_r: seeing a spike of CUDA OOMs on 6 nodes, weirdly headroom metric still shows ~350MB free on most GPUs. stacktrace: ```RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 256.00 MiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 39.20 GiB already allocated; 350.00 MiB free; 512.00 MiB reserved in HEADROOM)```

mike_r: logs show a bunch of reserved-block checks and then fragmentation reports. Not a simple large allocation. Possibly allocator fragmentation + KV cache pinning.

infra-rotation: on it. I pinged samir for allocator insights. Quick checks: `kubectl get pods -l pool=gpu-pool-c -o wide` and `nvidia-smi` on the flagged nodes.

liz_m: FYI one customer was paged by alpha-monitoring about degraded latency on embedding requests. CS already triaged.

samir_k: allocator note — we still have old reserve policy enabled on these nodes (dynamic_reserve=0.15, spare_pool=0.05). That combination can leave lots of small pinned blocks. If KV cache is heavy, we can hit fragmentation where logical free != usable contiguous.

infra-rotation: trying quick mitigation: 1) tell router to shift 30% of traffic off pool-c to pool-b, 2) set kvcache.writeback=false on the pool (to reduce new pinned allocations), 3) increase dynamic_reserve to 0.25 as emergency to prevent churn — applying now.

infra-rotation: command run: ```sh
# shift routing
curl -X POST https://router.internal/api/shift -d '{"from":"pool-c","to":"pool-b","percent":30}'
# patch pool config
redwoodctl pools patch pool-c --set kvcache.writeback=false --set dynamic_reserve=0.25
```

mike_r: doing a rolling restart of runtime pods on the 6 affected nodes with `--grace-period=30` to force allocator to free ghost reserves. Doing 2 at a time.

oncall-bot: Severity bumped to SEV-2 (customer impact). Incident channel created: #inc-2061234567.

cs-ops-bot: AlphaCorp and BetaProducts reported latency > 2x for embedding endpoints between 10:02 and 10:21 UTC. No 5xxs yet. Notifying AMs.

samir_k: quick analysis snippet from metrics: ```
metric: gpu_headroom_bytes
pool-c: mean=420000000, p50=360000000, p95=800000000
metric: contiguous_free_bytes
pool-c: mean=120000000, p50=80000000, p95=160000000
# indicates fragmentation: contiguous free << headroom
```

liz_m: good call on routing. Customers on pool-b see normal. We'll keep shift until we confirm allocator behavior.

infra-rotation: after rolling restarts, OOM counts dropped by ~85% on nodes we restarted. One node still spiking — investigating kernel logs: ```dmesg | tail -n 40
[10000.123] nvidia: GPU 2: mmap fail attempt, reserved block pinned
```

mike_r: for the remaining node I forced eviction of the kv cache process and restarted the runtime container. That cleared the pinned blocks, GPU recovered.

ops_lead: summary for operational handoff: cause likely allocator fragmentation amplified by KV cache pinning and low contiguous_free. Headroom metric didn't account for contiguous fragmentation. Immediate mitigations: routing shift, disable kvcache.writeback for pool-c, rolling restart/evict problematic pods, increase reserve threshold as temporary guard.

ops_lead: next steps (post-incident): 1) add contiguous_free_bytes to alerting with a headroom/contiguous ratio threshold, 2) refine reserve policy to avoid small pinned-block fragmentation (experiment with coalescing/pool compaction), 3) add a runtime action to quickly purge KV cache pinned blocks without full restart, 4) run a capacity audit for other pools.

mike_r: filing a quick PR with the runtime change: `reduce_dynamic_reserve_on_oom_hotfix` to add fallback allocation path and a tuned compaction pass. Canary deploying to pool-d in 10m.

cs-ops-bot: Noted affected customers; CS team drafting templated update. No refunds yet; will escalate if errors surface.

ops_lead: I'm taking oncall for the next 6 hours. infra-rotation, leave your notes in the incident doc and handoff checklist. If any node flaps again, trigger the immediate rollback (router shift back to pool-b).

infra-rotation: handoff ack. I'll update runbook with the eviction commands and a diagnostic snippet for contiguous free computation.

mike_r: monitoring traces now show request latency returning to baseline for alpha and beta. Will remain on-watch for 45m.

oncall-bot: Incident 2061234567 — status: mitigated, SEV-2 -> monitoring. Please continue chatter in #inc-2061234567 for follow-ups.

ops_lead: thanks team. We'll schedule a postmortem and include allocation engineers to look at long-term fixes. Leaving the channel open for cleanup notes.
